newsitem.title: USA: Stone sells forest products assets.
newsitem.headline: Stone sells forest products assets.

text.p: Stone Container Corp. said Thursday it had sold most of its non-core forest products operations to U.S. Forest Industries Inc., a new corporation formed by management of the division and an investment group.
Stone said it expected to take an estimated $10 million after-tax charge in the third quarter as a result of the sale.

Sales of these assets, along with the previously announced liquidation of certain other forest products assets, are expected to provide proceeds in excess of $100 million, most of it in cash, Stone said.
Stone said it will use the proceeds primarily to repay and reduce outstanding debt.
The latest sale included operations that produce and sell a variety of wood products, including softwood lumber, plywood, wood chips and veneer. Their revenues exceeded $100 million in 1995.
Stone's fiber procurement operations, which provide the essential raw materials for its paper mills, were not sold.
Stone said the sale will allow it to concentrate on core areas of containerboard, corrugated containers, paper bags and sacks, market pulp, and newsprint and groundwood papers.
Chicago-based Stone's stock rose 62.5 cents to $14.375 on the New York Stock Exchange in early afternoon trading.
